images.title: Stations on a route
images.purpose: Show distances measured from the same start: Station Q at 340 km and Station R at 615 km, the stretch from Q to R of 275 km and the route to R of 615 km.
images.composition: A route line from the first station with two stations, one bracket for the whole route and one for the stretch between Q and R.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. ROUTE: one horizontal line from x 128 to x 1328 at y 440 (1 km is 1.714 px) with an arrow head at the right end. STATIONS: exactly 3 filled circles 36 px across on the line: a green #009E73 circle at x 128 labelled below in 40 px First station 0 km, a teal #0072B2 circle at x 711 labelled below Station Q 340 km, and an amber #E69F00 circle at x 1182 labelled below Station R 615 km. WHOLE ROUTE: one grey #6B7280 bracket above the line from x 128 to x 1182 at y 330 with short end strokes and the label route to R = 615 km above it in 44 px bold at x 655, y 280. STRETCH: one reddish purple #CC79A7 bracket under the line from x 711 to x 1182 at y 600 with short end strokes and the label 615 − 340 = 275 km under it in 48 px bold at x 946, y 650. In all: 1 route line, 3 stations, 2 brackets. All shapes are flat fills with thin dark #2B2B2B outlines (3 px), no shadows and no gradients; all text is dark #1F2937 sans-serif. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Distances are measured from the same start, so the distance between two stations is the difference.
images.description: A route line with the first station at 0 km, Station Q at 340 km and Station R at 615 km, and 615 − 340 = 275 km between Q and R.
images.context: Concept image for Distance Between Two Stations. It follows the idea of the Longest Train Journey table in your maths book (distances from Dibrugarh) and shows the concept's own example of Station Q and Station R (practice values).
images.teaching_notes: Let the student see that both distances start at the same place. The slip to watch: adding 340 and 615.
